title: Dehydration — symptoms and when to seek help
content: Symptoms of dehydration include feeling thirsty, a headache, feeling light-headed or dizzy, dark yellow strong-smelling urine, peeing less often than usual, feeling tired, and a dry mouth, lips and tongue. Seek urgent help (GP or NHS 111) if you feel unusually tired or drowsy, feel dizzy on standing that does not go away, or have dark urine or reduced urination. Call 999 or go to A&E if there is blue, grey, pale or blotchy skin, lips or tongue, skin that feels cold, difficulty breathing or fast breathing, confusion, or if the person is sleepier than normal or difficult to wake — these can indicate shock, a serious complication of dehydration.
